newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's Krka sees 10 pct rise in 96 net profit.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's Krka sees 10 pct rise in 96 net profit.

text.p: Slovenian drug producer Krka said on Monday it expected 1996 net profit to be some 10 percent higher than the 2.9 billion tolars ($19.6 million) posted in 1995.
"Our profit has risen because of higher sales and lower costs," Krka's spokeswoman Janja Pozar said.

She said the company, which will list its shares on the OTC market of the Ljubljana bourse on February 10, plans to pay its first dividend this year, but added the dividend will only be determined at the shareholders meeting in June.
Sales rose to $313 million in 1996 from $294.1 million in 1995. Exports jumped to $223 million from $183 million.
"We registered the highest increase in exports to Russia and other former Soviet Union republics, to Poland and the Czech republic," Pozar said.
In Slovenia, Krka has a market share of 27 percent, on a par with rival pharmaceutical company Lek.
On Monday shares of Krka, which have a nominal value of 4,000 tolars, were traded at about 13,100 tolars in the grey market. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
